clues: It was a pre-Islamic practice.

clues: It is a share.

clues: It is a term from Islamic law.

The Qur'an says, "Do not transgress them."

hard.explain: The Qur'an says, "These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them." Jurists use hudud for the fixed penalties.

clues: It is a name of the Fire.
It is named in Surah Al-Qari'ah.
It is for the one whose scales are light.
The Qur'an calls it his mother.
It is called a blazing fire.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Qari'ah says whoever's scales are light, his mother will be Hawiyah, a raging fire.

clues: It is a valley named in the Qur'an.
It is called sacred.
A prophet was told to take off his sandals there.

Allah spoke to Musa there.
hard.explain: Allah told Musa, "Take off your sandals, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa."

clues: It is a small valley.

clues: It is next to the Ka'bah.

It was set by the Prophet ﷺ himself.

hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ set Yalamlam as the miqat for the people of Yemen.

clues: It is a place north west of Makkah, near the coast.

It was set by the Prophet ﷺ himself.

hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ set al-Juhfah as the miqat for the people of al-Sham.

clues: It is a building in Jerusalem.

It was completed in 72 AH.

hard.explain: The Dome of the Rock was built by Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan and completed in 72 AH. It stands in the al-Aqsa precinct.

clues: It was an institution in Baghdad.

Its name means "the House of Wisdom".
hard.explain: Bayt al-Hikmah in Abbasid Baghdad was a library and centre of translation, especially under al-Ma'mun.

clues: It is a mosque and a place of learning.

It became a great centre of Sunni learning after the Fatimid era.
It is one of the oldest universities in the world.
hard.explain: Al-Azhar was founded in Cairo in the 4th century AH. It became a centre of Sunni scholarship after the Fatimid era.

clues: It is a mosque in Madinah.
It belonged to the tribe of Banu Salimah.
Something changed while people were praying there.
They turned round in the middle of the prayer.
Its name means "the mosque of the two qiblahs".
hard.explain: Masjid al-Qiblatayn in Madinah is associated with the change of qiblah from Jerusalem to the Ka'bah.

clues: It was a building in Madinah.

They asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray in it.
Allah told him never to stand in it.

clues: They are mentioned in the Qur'an twice.

The Qur'an asks if Quraysh are better than them.

hard.explain: Surah Ad-Dukhan asks, "Are they better, or the people of Tubba' and those before them? We destroyed them."

clues: They are mentioned in the Qur'an.
They are mentioned twice.
They are listed with 'Ad and Thamud.

hard.explain: Surah Al-Furqan mentions 'Ad, Thamud and the dwellers of al-Rass among the nations destroyed after denying the messengers.

clues: They are mentioned in the Qur'an.
Shu'ayb was sent to them.
They cheated in measure.
They were destroyed by the punishment of the day of the shadow.
Their name means "the people of the thicket".
hard.explain: Surah Ash-Shu'ara says the dwellers of the wood (al-Aykah) denied the messengers when Shu'ayb told them to give full measure.

clues: They were from Bani Isra'il.
They lived in a town by the sea.
Fish came to them openly on one day of the week.
They broke a command by trapping them.
They were turned into apes.
hard.explain: The Qur'an tells of the town by the sea whose people broke the Sabbath by trapping fish. They were told, "Be apes, despised."

clues: He is mentioned in Surah Ya-Sin.
He came from the far end of a town.
He told his people to follow the messengers.
He said, "I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me."
On entering Paradise he wished his people knew how Allah had forgiven him.
hard.explain: Surah Ya-Sin tells of a man who came running from the far end of the city urging his people to follow the messengers. When told to enter Paradise, he wished his people knew.

clues: He is mentioned in Surah Ghafir.
He hid his faith.
He spoke up when Fir'awn wanted to kill Musa.
He asked, "Will you kill a man because he says my Lord is Allah?"
He was from the family of Fir'awn himself.
hard.explain: Surah Ghafir tells of a believing man of Fir'awn's family, who had hidden his faith, defending Musa.

clues: Their story is in Surah Al-Ma'idah.
Each offered a sacrifice.
Only one was accepted.
One killed the other.
A raven showed the killer how to bury his brother.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ma'idah tells the story of the two sons of Adam. Allah sent a raven to show the killer how to hide his brother's body.

clues: Their story is in Surah Al-Qalam.
They swore to harvest their fruit early in the morning.
They did not say "in sha' Allah".
They meant to keep the poor away.
They found their garden burned and black.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Qalam tells of the owners of a garden who planned to harvest it without giving the poor, and found it destroyed overnight.

clues: His story is in Surah Al-Kahf.
He had two gardens with a river between them.
He told his friend, "I have more wealth than you."
He thought his garden would never perish.
He ended up wringing his hands over what he had spent on it.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Kahf gives the parable of two men, one given two gardens. He boasted, and his fruit was destroyed.

hard.answer: The man who died for a hundred years
options: The man who died for a hundred years
clues: His story is in Surah Al-Baqarah.
He passed by a town in ruins.
He asked how Allah could bring it back to life.
Allah caused him to die and then raised him.
His food had not spoiled, but his donkey had turned to bones.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Baqarah tells of the man who passed a ruined town. Allah made him die for a hundred years and then raised him, as a sign.

clues: It was a gift to a prophet.

Its evening journey was a month's travel too.

hard.answer: The coats of mail of Dawud
options: The coats of mail of Dawud
clues: It was a skill given to a prophet.
Iron was made soft for him.
Allah told him to measure the links well.

hard.explain: Allah made iron soft for Dawud and taught him to make coats of mail to protect people in battle.

clues: It is a term of hadith science.

Most hadith fall into it.
It does not reach the level of tawatur.
It can still be sahih.

clues: It is a grade of hadith.

It can be caused by a broken chain or a weak narrator.
It means weak.

clues: It is a grade of hadith.
It is accepted as evidence.
It sits between sahih and da'if.
Its narrators are reliable but some are less precise.
Al-Tirmidhi used it very often.
hard.explain: A hasan hadith has a connected chain of trustworthy narrators whose precision is slightly below that of a sahih hadith.

clues: It is a grade of hadith.
It is the highest grade of acceptance.
Its chain is connected throughout.
Its narrators are upright and precise, with no hidden defect.
It means authentic or sound.
hard.explain: A sahih hadith has a connected chain of upright, precise narrators and is free of irregularity and hidden defects.

clues: It is one category of tawhid as scholars explain it.

Every messenger called his people to it.

hard.explain: Every messenger said, "Worship Allah, you have no god but Him." Al-Fatihah says, "You alone we worship."

clues: It is one category of tawhid as scholars explain it.

"There is nothing like Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing" sums it up.
hard.explain: Surah Ash-Shura says, "There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearer, the Seer."

clues: It was fought in the time of Umar.

Al-Husayn ibn Ali was martyred there.
